title: Object outlines
prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Create an original HNDRD sports product iconography CONCEPT BOARD, not a website or UI. Requested canvas 1600 x 1200, landscape 4:3. Input image is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: study the three thin black pictorial line icons along the bottom of the user's On screenshot. Closely preserve that airy, elegant illustrative line-art character, visual weight, generous negative space and specificity of subject. Draw original HNDRD sports icons, do not copy On's paths, shoe silhouette, logos, proprietary cloud sole or branding. Pure white background, black strokes, no colors, shadows, fills, gradients, decoration, card backgrounds or cartoon exaggeration. Nominal drawing grammar: 80 x 80 icon box, 2-unit consistent black stroke, round/carefully joined lines. A few dotted guides only where useful. Labels in a simple readable sans serif (Figtree-like), all-caps, black, small. Title at top left "HNDRD / PRODUCT ICONOGRAPHY" and concept subtitle beneath, generous top and bottom margins. Main board exactly 12 evenly spaced cells arranged 4 COLUMNS x 3 ROWS. Each cell shows one clearly legible icon about 90-110px high and its exact label below; no visible boxes around cells. Very light thin horizontal rules separate the three rows. Reading order labels: row 1 "WEIGHT", "BALANCE", "SHAFT FLEX", "MAX TENSION"; row 2 "STRING GAUGE", "STRING CONSTRUCTION", "OUTSOLE", "SUPPORT STRUCTURE"; row 3 "VENTILATION", "COMPARTMENTS", "SHOE STORAGE", "BAG DIMENSIONS". These are ATTRIBUTE SUBJECTS, not product claims. Do not invent any product measurements, ratings or model names. Shaft flex and tension must be clearly different: flex bends a long slender badminton racket SHAFT, tension pulls the racket STRING BED. Gauge means strand DIAMETER, not length. Support structure refers to a shoe's midfoot structure, not arch anatomy. Compartments means divisions inside a bag; shoe storage means a separate shoe-containing area. Add restrained footer "CONCEPT ARTWORK / ORIGINAL HNDRD DRAWINGS / PRODUCT VALUES NOT ASSIGNED". Footer also includes a compact legibility sample: repeat the BALANCE icon small, medium, large under labels "32", "48", "80"; these are presentation-size targets, not product values. Keep every label spelled correctly, full icons in frame, equal optical scale. This is one standalone concept, never a collage of alternative boards.

Concept subtitle exactly "OBJECT OUTLINES". Use recognisable whole objects with very few internal lines, close to the reference's lacing, feather and heel diagram. WEIGHT: an elegant original feather to signify the weight attribute, no speed trails. BALANCE: side-profile badminton racket resting on a small triangular fulcrum under its shaft, the racket head at left, grip at right. SHAFT FLEX: long slim racket with subtly bowed shaft, straight dotted reference line alongside. MAX TENSION: frontal racket head with sparse string grid and tiny outward arrows at four sides. STRING GAUGE: one strand shown as two parallel outlines with short measurement ticks ACROSS its width. STRING CONSTRUCTION: short filament bundle with three distinguishable filaments visible at one end. OUTSOLE: simple bottom-view court shoe sole with a few tread lines. SUPPORT STRUCTURE: side view of court shoe with one clean midfoot support shape visible. VENTILATION: outline mesh patch with just three soft airflow lines passing through. COMPARTMENTS: slightly open kitbag showing three simple separated storage spaces. SHOE STORAGE: independent zip shoe pouch containing a small shoe profile. BAG DIMENSIONS: side-profile racket kitbag, external length and height measurement marks with no numeric measurements. Keep drawings gentle and illustrative, minimal internal detail.
reference_role: Style reference only; attached in referenced_image_paths
